_provenance: The owner approved this standard for addiction-recovery ONLY. Extending it to the other nine was my own judgement and the owner flagged that as a decision that was theirs to make — some of these meaningfully narrow the candidate pool. Until confirmed or trimmed, this file does NOT constrain batches: treat entries other than addiction-recovery as a proposal, not a rule.
_comment: Categories where acting on bad advice can cause physical harm, delay treatment someone needs, or worsen a crisis. The bar is higher here and an empty category is explicitly preferred to an adjacent one: a bad recommendation costs more than an absent one. Owner's ruling, made about addiction-recovery and generalised. Adding a category here raises the standard; it never lowers one.

categories.addiction-recovery: Dependence, withdrawal and relapse. Wrong or moralising advice can keep someone from treatment, and some withdrawal is medically dangerous.
categories.therapy-literacy: How to find and judge therapy. Bad guidance here can send someone to the wrong modality or away from help entirely.
categories.anxiety-management: Overlaps with clinical anxiety disorders. Technique content presented as treatment can delay real care.
categories.emotional-regulation: Frequently reached for in genuine distress rather than for self-improvement.
categories.grief-and-loss: People arrive acutely bereaved. Prescriptive stage models and timelines do measurable harm.
categories.injury-rehab: Loading an injury wrongly causes further injury. Anything here is education, never assessment.
categories.back-pain-management: The category most likely to attract confident structural claims that frighten people out of moving.
categories.hormonal-health: Testing and treatment decisions with real medical consequences, and a heavy supplement-marketing presence.
categories.fat-loss: Adjacent to disordered eating. Aggressive deficit and body-composition content can be actively harmful.
categories.supplements-literacy: Dose and interaction errors have physical consequences, and the field is almost entirely commercial.

standard: Prefer a documented empty category to an adjacent or under-credentialed creator.
A creator here should normally carry the `credentialed` signal, or the record must say plainly why they are trustworthy without it.
`notFor` and `caveats` must state the limit explicitly — that this is education and not assessment or treatment.
A creator whose framing discourages professional help needs that named in their record, not softened.
